subject: DPA / GDPR migration playbook: redline cascade and legal cadence
messages:
From: Lydia Chan <lydia.chan@novacorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novacorp Legal <legal@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Proposed DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is Novacorp's redline of Redwood's standard DPA — the main asks are around (1) explicit export-control carveouts for our EU subsidiaries, (2) an expanded incident notification SLA, and (3) processor-subprocessor routing commitments tied to our contractual SLOs.

We flagged the SCCs replacement clause and a new transfer-impact addendum that our privacy team prefers to see in the MSA/Order Form. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept:
- a narrow export-control carveout limited to regulatory blocking actions,
- 48-hour initial incident acknowledgement (we pushed for 24 but can be flexible), and
- subprocessor routing that preserves our ability to approve certain classes of subprocessors?

For context I included a short export-risk footprint (spreadsheet) showing the regions where data residency will matter. We'd like to finalize redlines before the commercial signoff planned for the end of July.

Attachments: [Novacorp_DPA_redline.docx (docx, 42KB)], [export-risk-footprint.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)]

Best,
Lydia Chan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data
Novacorp
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Chan <lydia.chan@novacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:28:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Hi Lydia — thanks for the detailed packet and the export footprint. I'm looping in Ben (contracts/procurement) and Jordan (legal ops) so we can coordinate a single redline response and a small migration playbook that ties DPA clauses to the Order Form routing.

Quick answers up front:
- Export-control carveout: Redwood's position is to accept a narrowly scoped regulatory block carveout if Novacorp provides explicit language limiting the carveout to country-level legal prohibitions and includes a notice & mitigation cooperation clause.
- Incident acknowledgement: we can agree to 48 hours for initial acknowledgement. We'll keep 24 hrs as an internal SLO for escalation.
- Subprocessor approvals: we can offer a class-based approval right (e.g., AI hosting, logging providers) rather than per-subprocessor sign-off — that tends to be faster for operations.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Ben to produce a redline summary mapping each external ask to our acceptance/reject/conditional list.
2) Jordan to prepare a short Order Form addendum template (transfer-impact addendum) we can present to Novacorp legal.
3) I will put together a brief migration playbook (how this affects hosting routing, SCCs, and the fallback plan) for Novacorp's ops.

Can we aim for a consolidated redline response by EOD Wednesday (23 Jun)? If Novacorp needs faster turnaround, tell me what you can accept.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Lydia Chan <lydia.chan@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Karthik / Lydia — thanks for the note. I reviewed Novacorp's redline and put together a short decision matrix. Summary here (full mapping attached as PDF):
- Export-control carveout: ACCEPT CONDITIONAL — require specific limiting language + 30-day cure window for operational impacts.
- Incident SLA: ACCEPT (48-hr ack; 72-hr substantive update; full post-mortem within 30 days).
- SCCs clause: ACCEPT with edit to allow Redwood's maintained SCCs + fallbacks to equivalent protections when update windows occur.
- Subprocessor routing: COUNTERPROPOSE — class-based approval with a quarterly notify/objection cadence (if Novacorp objects to a class, they must escalate within 10 business days).

Attachments: [redline-summary.pdf (pdf, 18KB)]
HubSpot: HS-2109847 (I added notes and linked the shared drive). Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3cNovacorp-DPA

If that alignment looks good, Jordan can draft the Order Form transfer-impact addendum to reflect the carveouts and the fallback routing policy. I also flagged potential pricing implications for dedicated hosting in the EU if strict per-subprocessor approvals are insisted upon — we should surface that now.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Contracts & Procurement
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Proposed DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Jordan — forwarding Novacorp's packet and Ben's decision matrix. Please prepare:
- A slim transfer-impact addendum (one page) we can insert into the Order Form that captures the export-control carveout language and the SCCs maintenance/fallback.
- A clean redline of our DPA accepting the incident SLA and the class-based subprocessor counterproposal.
- A short note to commercial on potential cost delta if Novacorp insists on per-subprocessor approvals.

We will accept the 48-hour incident acknowledgement and the 72-hour substantive update.

Please send the consolidated redline + the transfer-impact addendum and we'll route to internal procurement for final signoff. Once both are agreed, I'll issue the DocuSign envelope (I will copy dse@docusign.net).
